top_level_objectives: Understand vectors as quantities with magnitude and direction.
Apply vector addition and decomposition to analyze projectile motion.
Recognize the independence of horizontal and vertical motion in projectile trajectories.
Predict how changes in launch conditions affect projectile range and maximum height.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of vector addition using a tip-to-tail graphical method.
key_visuals: Two distinct vectors represented by arrows in AR space.
A third vector representing the resultant, formed by placing the tail of the second vector at the tip of the first.
student_actions: Observe the visualization of two vectors and their resultant.
Manipulate the initial vectors to see how the resultant changes.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how a vector can be decomposed into horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components using a right triangle.
key_visuals: A single vector in AR space.
Dashed lines indicating the x and y axes.
Right triangle formed by the vector and its components on the axes.
student_actions: Observe the visualization of a vector and its components.
Rotate the original vector and observe how its components change.
See the magnitudes of the components and original vector labeled, along with angles.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of projectile motion and its initial velocity vector.
key_visuals: A projectile launch point in AR space.
An initial velocity vector shown at the launch point, with adjustable magnitude and angle.
student_actions: Adjust the magnitude and angle of the initial velocity vector.

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the initial velocity of a projectile.
key_visuals: The initial velocity vector from the previous scene.
Decomposed horizontal (vx) and vertical (vy) components shown originating from the launch point.
Labels for vx and vy magnitudes.
student_actions: Observe the decomposed initial velocity components.
Note that vx remains constant and vy changes over time.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the independence of horizontal and vertical motion.
key_visuals: A projectile following a parabolic path.
Two ghost projectiles, one moving with only horizontal velocity, the other with only vertical velocity (under gravity).
Trajectories of the ghost projectiles shown alongside the actual projectile's path.
student_actions: Observe how the actual projectile's position at any time corresponds to the combined positions of the two ghost projectiles.
Confirm that the horizontal motion is constant and the vertical motion is uniformly accelerated.

scenes.brief_purpose: Allow students to explore how launch conditions affect projectile trajectory, range, and maximum height.
key_visuals: Adjustable sliders or input fields for initial speed and launch angle.
Readouts for range and maximum height.
student_actions: Change the initial speed and launch angle.
Observe the resulting changes in the projectile's trajectory, range, and maximum height.
Record observations or answer questions about the relationships observed.
